associations.name: Brom Martikov
associations.relationship: Arabelle has feelings for Brom. He saved her during the battle at the Festival of Light.

associations.name: Madam Eva
associations.relationship: Madam Eva is the spiritual leader of the Vistani. Arabelle grew up hearing her stories.

name: Arabelle Vanduva
description: Arabelle Vanduva is Luvash's 16-year-old daughter. She was kidnapped by the hags of Old Bonegrinder and rescued by the adventurers. She is quiet, watchful, and not cute — she notices details adults miss and says simple things that land hard because she is not trying to impress anyone. She came home when other children did not, and that changed how the whole camp sees her. At the Festival of Light, she arrived with Luvash and the Vistani wagons, and Brom Martikov saved her during the battle.
dm_notes: Arabelle should not feel like "the missing quest child." She came home when other children did not, and that changes how the whole camp sees her. She wants to feel normal again, though she probably cannot name that. She knows a child's version of the truth — which can be more useful than an adult's. She has feelings for Brom Martikov, who saved her at the Festival of Light. The party rescued her from Old Bonegrinder, and the early Tser Pool scenes had her wide-eyed and fascinated by the heroes.

associations.name: Prince Ian Frostmantle
associations.relationship: Geoffrey’s nephew and the heir to the throne. Geoffrey is fiercely protective of him and carried him through the woods after the ambush.

associations.name: Mistress Clarissa Allyson
associations.relationship: Geoffrey sent the party to find Clarissa with a sealed letter bearing his signet ring. He trusts her knowledge and wisdom.

associations.name: Ser Brennor Cale
associations.relationship: One of Geoffrey’s knights who survived the undead ambush and made it to the church. After Father Alric’s death, Brennor led the remaining survivors to White Bridge.

name: Lord Geoffrey Frostmantle
description: Lord Geoffrey Frostmantle is the younger brother of the King of Damara and the Lord of Westwatch, Protector of the Western Reaches. A capable warrior and commander, Geoffrey was the second-born son of the Frostmantle dynasty and was sent to train and lead the family’s forces in the Western Reaches. He is fiercely loyal to his brother the King and devoted to his nephew Prince Ian. The party first encountered Geoffrey on the banks of the Pelavir River, dragging his gravely wounded nephew from the wreckage of an undead ambush.
dm_notes:
Geoffrey led a force of 60 men (20 knights and 40 men-at-arms) toward Valls after reports of monsters and demonic creatures slaughtering villages and farms. They crossed the river north of the City of Valls and posted 20 men to guard the bridge as a retreat path. The force was ambushed by undead led by a dark rider and overwhelmed within minutes. As Prince Ian fell, Geoffrey and a few remaining knights formed a defensive perimeter. Geoffrey got the Prince onto his horse and rode, but the horse was killed and both fell. Geoffrey carried the gravely wounded Prince through the woods overnight, evading enemies, until they heard the Night Screamer attack on the Sea Spray.

Geoffrey gave the party a sealed letter bearing his signet ring to take to Mistress Clarissa Allyson in Valls, asking her to share what she knows about the spreading darkness. He then returned to White Bridge with Captain Reaven’s crew, escorting the wounded Prince to safety.

Geoffrey knows Clarissa well through the Damaran court but they are not close friends the way Clarissa and the King are — Geoffrey was raised apart from the capital, trained in the Western Reaches. His loyalty to his brother and nephew is absolute.

associations.name: Lord Geoffrey Frostmantle
associations.relationship: Ian’s uncle. Geoffrey carried Ian through the woods after the undead ambush and ensured his survival.

associations.name: Mistress Clarissa Allyson
associations.relationship: Ian and Clarissa are romantically involved, on and off. Clarissa trusted the party only after seeing the letter proving they were sent by the Crown.

associations.name: Ser Brennor Cale
associations.relationship: One of the knights sworn to Ian’s service who survived the ambush and led survivors to White Bridge.

name: Prince Ian Frostmantle
description: Prince Ian Frostmantle is the eldest son of the King of Damara and heir to the Frostmantle dynasty. A young paladin trained in the martial and divine traditions, he was gravely wounded during the Night Screamer attack on the Sea Spray in Session 02 and carries an unknown curse linked to Tharizdun’s growing influence. When a healer attempted to mend his wounds, the magic was repelled by an impenetrable wall of darkness, and the Prince seized the healer’s wrist with unnatural strength, triggering terrifying visions.
dm_notes:
Prince Ian was aboard the Sea Spray when it was attacked by Night Screamers during Session 02. He was gravely wounded and carries an unknown curse linked to Tharizdun’s growing influence — healing magic is repelled by a wall of darkness when applied to him, and physical contact triggered disturbing visions for the healer Sage. His uncle Lord Geoffrey carried him through the woods after the ambush and the Sea Spray crew escorted them both to White Bridge for safety.

Ian is romantically involved with Mistress Clarissa Allyson, on and off. The letter Geoffrey gave the party was signed with Ian’s authority, and Clarissa would not share her knowledge until the players presented it as proof they were sent by the Crown.

associations.name: Shorthagot, Harbinger of Ruin
associations.relationship: Shorthagot is the avatar of Tharizdun, trapped in the Great Machine he helped the Netherese create. Lyzara'Nualith is attempting to free him so he can complete his work and free their master, Tharizdun.

associations.name: Strahd Von Zarovich
associations.relationship: Lyzara sought out Strahd after learning he possesses the Lode Stone, one of the four Keys. After being trapped in Barovia by the Mist, she presented herself as his representative while pursuing her own agenda. She convinced him the Vistani had betrayed him, leading to the attacks on the Vistani camps.

associations.name: Mistress Clarissa Allyson
associations.relationship: Direct nemesis. Clarissa never trusted Elysra from the moment she arrived in Valls. Lyzara knew Clarissa was head of the Order of the Yellow Rose and knew the Key's location. She tortured Clarissa beneath the Citadel using a mind-rending creature to extract the Key's whereabouts.

associations.name: Tharizdun, The Chained God
associations.relationship: Lyzara'Nualith's true master. Everything she does — the infiltration of Valls, the assault on the Citadel, the pursuit of the Keys — serves Tharizdun's liberation.

associations.name: Lord Edmund Williams
associations.relationship: Her husband, whom she corrupted and ultimately murdered to gain control of Valls and access the vaults beneath the Citadel when Clarissa blocked her access.

associations.name: LeJean
associations.relationship: The Constable of Valls who served her. She stabbed him with a dark dagger and transformed him into the Jailer as punishment for his betrayal.

associations.name: The Abbot
associations.relationship: Lady Williams convinced Strahd that the Vistani had betrayed him. Strahd then ordered her to have the Abbot deal with them, resulting in the assaults on the Tser Pool and Tser Hill Vistani camps.

name: Lady Elysra Nivariel Williams
description: Lady Elysra Nivariel Williams is the primary antagonist of the campaign — a succubus named Lyzara'Nualith who infiltrated Damaran high society by taking the human form and name Elysra Nivariel. She arrived in Valls presenting herself as a widow of minor Damaran nobility and entered the service of Lady Meagana Williams. She poisoned Meagana and, while the woman was wasting away, comforted and corrupted Lord Edmund Williams during his grief — eventually marrying him and dropping her maiden name. Beautiful, charming, and politically astute, she spent years positioning herself to access the secrets beneath the Citadel of the Yellow Rose. She orchestrated the Fall of Valls in 1496 DR, personally led the assault on the Citadel, and now operates within Barovia — trapped by the Mist after tricking Lady Fiona Wachter and others into summoning her through it. In human guise she is indistinguishable from a mortal noblewoman, but her true nature is revealed in moments of rage — her eyes flare with madness, a violet glow of abyssal power curls around her hands, and her voice fills the room with fanatic intensity.
dm_notes:
Lyzara'Nualith is a succubus in service to Tharizdun, the Chained God. Her ultimate goal is to free Shorthagot — Tharizdun's avatar — from the Great Machine beneath the ruins of Thul Avenar (now the Monastery of the Yellow Rose), so that Shorthagot can complete his work and free their master.

INFILTRATION OF VALLS: Lyzara arrived in Valls under the human identity of Elysra Nivariel, presenting as a widow of minor Damaran nobility. She entered the employ of Lady Meagana Williams, wife of Lord Edmund Williams — a close friend of King Frostmantle and Clarissa Allyson. She slowly poisoned Meagana, and while the woman wasted away, she comforted Edmund and corrupted his mind. After Meagana's death she married Edmund. Many suspected Elysra had a hand in Meagana's death, but none dared say so within earshot of Lord Williams.

She spent years studying the Citadel's old construction, walking halls that had been closed for generations, and asking clever questions about wards, the Yellow Rose, and the sealed chambers Clarissa had begun to unearth. Clarissa never trusted her. Father Alric later recalled: "There is power behind Lady Williams. Power that no grieving widow should wield."

She finally killed Edmund to gain control of Valls when Clarissa continued to block her access to the vaults and records beneath the Citadel.

THE FALL OF VALLS (1496 DR): Lady Williams led the assault on the Citadel of the Yellow Rose. Her forces breached the planar gateway beneath the city, flooding Valls with horrors from the Shadowfell. She personally oversaw the torture of Mistress Clarissa Allyson in the ruined chambers beneath the Citadel, using a mind-rending creature to extract the location of the Veilpiercer — one of the four Keys of Shorthagot. When the party intervened (Session 07), she released a wall of arcane energy to throw them back, then stabbed Constable LeJean with a dark dagger — "That is for your betrayal! Fool!" — transforming him into a 40-foot monstrosity called the Jailer. She opened a portal and vanished.

INSIDE BAROVIA: Lady Williams tricked Lady Fiona Wachter and other women into performing a ritual that summoned her into Barovia, allowing her to slip past the Mist and Strahd's initial notice. She did not realize this would also trap her within Barovia like anyone else. She sought out Strahd after learning he possesses the Lode Stone (the second Key) and presented herself as his representative while pursuing her own agenda. She wants the players to bring the Veilpiercer to the Great Machine and open it so she can make her attack.

At the Festival of Light in Vallaki (Session 26), she appeared uninvited and publicly delivered Strahd's message, mocking the festival. Mist rolled into the square and chaos erupted — Stella Wachter was killed by her minions during the attack. Afterward at the Blue Water Inn, she put a spell on Urwin Martikov, waited for the party, and offered a deal: turn over the Key and she will reveal the location of Strahd's Necromantic Anchor and transport them to the Amber Temple. She made clear the Artifact will be hers one way or the other. She will not start a fight no matter what the players say.

She convinced Strahd that the Vistani had betrayed him, and Strahd ordered her to have the Abbot deal with them — resulting in the massacre at Tser Pool and the assault on Tser Hill.

CONNECTION TO THE STREET URCHINS: Before the Fall of Valls, Constable LeJean ran the street urchins of the city. He sent one of them — Dagger — to steal from Lady Williams. Dagger was caught, and Lady Williams turned him into a dog as punishment.

ENDGAME: The final confrontation with Lyzara'Nualith takes place at the Monastery of the Yellow Rose / Tur Farael, at the entrance to the Infernal Machine. She will track the players there and attempt to take the Keys and use the Machine. If she activates it without all four Keys, powerful magic will tear through Faerûn before the Machine explodes, destroying much of the Dalelands. The players must stop her and use the Keys to prevent the explosion.

Her rallying cry: "YES! To shatter the wheel of suffering… to burn this wretched tapestry to ash!"

associations.name: Lady Elysra Nivariel Williams
associations.relationship: Edmund's second wife. The succubus Lyzara'Nualith poisoned his first wife Meagana, corrupted his mind during his grief, married him, and ultimately murdered him to gain control of Valls.

associations.name: Mistress Clarissa Allyson
associations.relationship: Childhood friend. Edmund, Clarissa, and King Frostmantle grew up together at court. Clarissa tried to protect the Citadel's secrets from Lady Williams but could not break through Edmund's corrupted loyalty.

name: Lord Edmund Williams
description: Lord Edmund Williams was a Damaran nobleman and the Lord of Valls — a childhood friend of King Frostmantle and Mistress Clarissa Allyson. He was a good man whose mind was corrupted by the succubus Lyzara'Nualith after she entered his household in the guise of Elysra Nivariel. His first wife, Lady Meagana Williams, was slowly poisoned by Lyzara while she was in Meagana's employ. As Meagana wasted away, Lyzara comforted Edmund and corrupted his mind, eventually marrying him. Many suspected Elysra had a hand in Meagana's death, but none dared say so within earshot of Lord Williams. He was ultimately murdered by his own wife when she needed to seize control of Valls and access the vaults and records beneath the Citadel of the Yellow Rose, which Clarissa had been blocking.
dm_notes:
Lord Edmund Williams was one of King Frostmantle's closest friends and allies. Along with Clarissa Allyson, the three grew up together at court. Edmund was a noble and honorable man who fell prey to a demon's manipulation — Lyzara'Nualith targeted his household specifically because of his position as Lord of Valls and his proximity to the Citadel of the Yellow Rose.

His first wife, Lady Meagana Williams, hired Elysra Nivariel as a servant or attendant. Lyzara used this position to slowly poison Meagana while simultaneously comforting the grieving Edmund and corrupting his mind. After Meagana's death, Edmund married Elysra. Father Alric recalled that she "captured Lord Williams' heart as his wife was slowly wasting away."

When Clarissa continued to block Elysra's access to the vaults and archives beneath the Citadel, Lyzara could wait no longer and killed Edmund to take direct control of Valls. His death is referenced in the campaign sources as "the deceased Lord Williams."

associations.name: Lady Elysra Nivariel Williams
associations.relationship: LeJean served Lady Williams as Constable of Valls. She stabbed him with a dark dagger and transformed him into the Jailer — a 40-foot monstrosity — as punishment for his betrayal.

name: LeJean
description: LeJean was the Constable of Valls who served Lady Elysra Williams. He ran the street urchins of the city, using them as a network of petty thieves. When Lady Williams fled the Citadel after torturing Mistress Clarissa Allyson, she stabbed LeJean with a dark dagger — "That is for your betrayal! Fool!" — and the blade melted into his body, transforming him into a 40-foot monstrosity known as the Jailer. The creature wielded a 20-foot whip made from a massive spine, and its rib cage formed an iron jail with screaming souls trapped inside. The party eventually brought the creature down.
dm_notes:
LeJean stood beside Lady Williams during the torture of Clarissa in the ruined chambers beneath the Citadel. The mind-rending creature used to interrogate Clarissa had its tendrils connected to both Clarissa and LeJean. When the party burst in and Lady Williams decided to flee through a portal, she stabbed LeJean as a final act — transforming him into the Jailer, a massive aberration the party had to fight (Session 07).

Before the Fall of Valls, LeJean ran the street urchins of the city. Among them was Dagger, whom LeJean sent to steal from Lady Williams. Dagger was caught, and Lady Williams turned him into a dog as punishment.

LeJean's "betrayal" that earned Elysra's wrath is left deliberately vague — it may refer to his failure to prevent the party from reaching the Citadel, or to some earlier act of defiance.

associations.name: Tharizdun, The Chained God
associations.relationship: Shorthagot is Tharizdun's avatar, birthed from the Abyss itself to embody his master's will. His sole purpose is to free the Chained God from his cosmic imprisonment.

associations.name: Lady Elysra Nivariel Williams
associations.relationship: Lyzara'Nualith serves Shorthagot's cause. She orchestrated the Fall of Valls to breach the planar gateway connected to his prison beneath the Infernal Machine, and now pursues the Keys needed to free him.

name: Shorthagot, Harbinger of Ruin
description: Shorthagot, Harbinger of Ruin, is Tharizdun’s avatar — a being birthed from the Abyss itself to embody the Chained God’s will. He is the ultimate threat behind the campaign’s events. In the age of Netheril, Shorthagot infiltrated the Empire’s highest circles disguised as Arthindol the Terraseer, one of Netheril’s most trusted archmages. He manipulated and corrupted the greatest arcane minds of Netheril into creating the Great Machine at Thul Avenar — a device he told them would let them access a new form of magic, but which was in truth designed to awaken Tharizdun. When champions of Faerûn rose to oppose him, they defeated Shorthagot and used the very machine he had devised to imprison him. Bound by divine, mechanical, and magical forces, Shorthagot was sealed into a displacement prison beyond space and time within the Infernal Machine. His prison is slowly weakening as the millennia have passed, and his influence seeps through the barriers between planes, corrupting everything it touches.
dm_notes:
ORIGINS: Shorthagot is an avatar of Tharizdun, the Chained God — one of the most terrifying entities in all existence. Tharizdun was imprisoned by the combined efforts of all other gods at the dawn of time after he created the Abyss and waged the Dawn War. Throughout history, his followers have sought to free him. Shorthagot was the most formidable of these agents.

THE NETHERESE DECEPTION: Shorthagot infiltrated the Empire of Netheril disguised as Arthindol the Terraseer. In these "humans" he saw an opportunity to finally complete his purpose. To free his master.. After embedding himself in the Empire's highest arcane circles. He oversaw multiple state-level arcane projects, including six scattered research sites called the Thul laboratories — imperial black laboratories hidden far from Netheril's heart so no rival could see the whole design. He worked to keep the truth from those that might stop him. It took more than two centuries to complete the work at these sites..
  • Thul Vharak (Mount Ghakis) — shielding, warding, containment fields
  • Thul Seyr — veil-piercing, planar contact, transport
  • Thul Mystren — mythallar crystal refinement and power-routing
  • Thul Karath — construct intelligence, automaton cores
  • Thul Oraph — long-range observation, divinatory mapping
  • Thul Avenar ("The Gate of the Horizon") — the central site where all research came together in the making of the Great Machine

Each site knew only part of the truth. Only Arthindol and a very small inner circle knew they were all building pieces of the same thing. He tempted the Netherese with the promise of a machine merging magic and technology that would let them access a new form of magic. It was all a lie — the Machine was designed to awaken Tharizdun.

THE IMPRISONMENT: Champions of Faerûn defeated Shorthagot and his allies. These allies called themselves the Order of the Yellow Rose. They used the very machine he had devised to imprison him. The Great Machine's harmonic lattice was reversed, collapsing Shorthagot's essence into a pocket dimension outside of space and time. Bound by mechanical and arcane forces, he was sealed into a displacement prison beyond space and time within the Machine itself.

THE SEAL: Seven arcanists survived the imprisonment. They concluded that destroying the Machine was impossible — its core was interwoven with the Aether well beneath the mountain. Removing it would destabilize the displacement prison containing Shorthagot. They collapsed the upper citadel, fused the mountain's strata with spellglass and obsidian, and inscribed a Seal keyed to harmonic comprehension. The entrance to Thul Avenar can be accessed using 4 powerful Artifacts.. The Machine was renamed the Infernal Machine after contact with Shorthagot and his imprisonment.

THE KEYS: Four artifacts — the Keys:
  1. The Heart of the Machine - a sphere 4" by 4" that contains a small amount of the essence of Shorthagot and is needed to communicate with Shorthagot.
  2. The Lode Stone — Used to manage access to realms or realities. Created by Netheril Empire.
  3. The Veilpiercer — pierces the veils between realities..
  4. The Kara'thrix Coil — stabilizes the energy of the other keys and is a powerful/modified Ioun Stone/Mythaller.

THE ORDER OF THE YELLOW ROSE: Founded just before the Fall of the Netheril Empire to stop Shorthagot from completing his work and freeing Tharizdun. They were successful, but at great cost as Shorthagot is a powerful foe. The Order swore an oath to keep the keys safe and the Infernal Machine as they call it, sealed forever.

CURRENT STATE: Shorthagot remains displaced in a non-localized interval beyond space and time. His prison is sustained indirectly by the altered architecture of the Infernal Machine. His influence slowly seeps through the weakening barriers. Lyzara'Nualith, his servant, is actively pursuing the Keys to restore the Machine's original configuration and reverse the displacement.

As recorded by the arcanist Kelith Omvaran: "The entity is not destroyed. It is imprisoned in The Infernal Machine beneath Túr-Pharael. If rediscovered by those driven by ambition rather than discipline, the consequences will impact everything and all things.

associations.name: Mistress Clarissa Allyson
associations.relationship: Alric's oldest student and close friend. Clarissa's torn missive addressed him as "my old friend" and entrusted him as the final guardian of the Key after Valls fell.

associations.name: Kaelin Stormraven
associations.relationship: Alric's killer. Kaelin disguised herself as a lost child and, once inside the Old Church, slit his throat without warning during Session 04.

associations.name: Ser Brennor Cale
associations.relationship: Brennor sheltered at the Old Church alongside Alric with survivors from Valls. After Alric's death, Brennor took command of the remaining survivors.

associations.name: Lady Elysra Nivariel Williams
associations.relationship: Alric was deeply suspicious of Lady Williams and shared critical intelligence about her with the party before his death — her knowledge of the Citadel's sealed chambers, her influence over Lord Williams, and the power he sensed behind her.

name: Father Alric Vendril
description: Father Alric Vendril was the First Sage of the Yellow Rose — a senior member of the Order and one of Mistress Clarissa Allyson's oldest friends and confidants. Gaunt and silver-haired, he looked more spirit than man, his face deeply lined with age and sorrow. He wore a simple, threadbare robe marked with the faded emblem of a sunburst and carried a battered iron rosary, the beads worn smooth by decades of prayer. Despite his frail frame, there was a quiet strength about him — a light that had not yet surrendered to the dark. His healing magic had faded over the years, limited to cantrips and lesser prayers, but his faith and wisdom remained steadfast. He was killed by Kaelin Stormraven during Session 04 at the Old Church near the West Road.
dm_notes:
ROLE IN THE ORDER: Father Alric was the First Sage of the Yellow Rose, a senior member of the Order who served beneath Mistress Clarissa Allyson. Clarissa knew him from when she was barely more than a scribe, and he watched her rise to rebuild the Order. Their bond was deep — her torn missive addressed him as "my old friend" and named him the final guardian of the Key.

THE FALL OF VALLS: During the Fall, Alric stayed in the lower quarters of the city tending to the sick and dying. He saw the mists rising first, curling through alleyways before the dead marched. He heard the bells of the Citadel toll once — and then never again. He fled with survivors and knights to the Old Church near the West Road, where he sheltered them alongside Ser Brennor Cale and a handful of battered knights.

INTELLIGENCE SHARED: Before his death, Alric provided the party with critical information:
  • On Lady Williams: "She knew too much of the Citadel's old construction. She walked halls that had been closed for generations. She asked clever questions about wards, the Yellow Rose, and the sealed chambers Clarissa had begun to unearth. Clarissa never trusted her."
  • On Clarissa: "A keen mind — sharper than any sword. She is a fortress of will. If she yet lives, she will not have fallen idly."
  • On the sealed chambers: "Some doors must remain sealed... some evils must never be woken."
  • He dreamed of the mist and heard voices in his sleep — a voice calling fragments of Tharizdun's name, which he recognized from ancient forbidden texts once locked in the temple library.

DEATH (Session 04): Kaelin Stormraven, disguised as a lost child the party had rescued from Hell Hounds, struck without warning. Her form twisted into a young woman, and in one smooth motion she slit Father Alric's throat, then vanished in a shimmer of arcane mist to attack Sage. The party fought and killed Kaelin, but Alric was already dead.

BURIAL (Session 05): Ser Brennor Cale arrived with three weathered knights. At Krutha's firm urging, Alric's body was given to flame to ensure no dark power could claim him. A prayer to Lathander, god of renewal and light, was offered. Brennor spoke: "He was a light in the dark, a comfort to the broken. Let his soul find peace where the shadows can no longer touch him."

LEGACY: Among the dead refugees on the West Road, the party found a bloodied, partially burned letter bearing the seal of the Yellow Rose — Clarissa's torn missive addressed to Alric. It revealed that Valls had fallen, that the Key had been sent east with Brother Caelis and the Dawn Guard, and that Alric was entrusted as its final guardian. He never received it. Brother Fridriec Embershade of the Verdant Heart druid enclave mourns Alric as a distant cousin.

associations.name: Ezmerelda d'Avenir
associations.relationship: Velinka's niece — daughter of Velinka's sister Sorina. Velinka believes all her family died when the Stormraven Sisters destroyed the Tser Pass Vistani at the Druid Clearing in Damara. She is unaware that Ezmerelda survived.

name: Velinka d'Avenir
description: Velinka d'Avenir is a Vistani woman originally of the Tser Pass Vistani and the d'Avenir family. She is the sister of Sorina d'Avenir and aunt of Ezmerelda. When the Stormraven Sisters attacked and wiped out the Tser Pass Vistani at the Druid Clearing in Damara — punishment for betraying Strahd — Velinka was pulled from the wreckage by druids of the Verdant Heart and nursed back to life. She believes all her family perished in the attack and is unaware that her niece Ezmerelda also survived. While recovering among the druids, Velinka experienced prophetic visions of Barovia burning beneath an unblinking red eye. She guided the party through the Devil's Mists to the Gates of Barovia during Session 09, opening the gates with Vistani blood but refusing to enter herself.
dm_notes:
BACKGROUND: Velinka was originally part of the Tser Pass Vistani, a caravan led by the d'Avenir family. Her sister Sorina was the heart of the caravan — strong, willful, and devoted to the old Vistani ways. The Stormraven Sisters destroyed the caravan at the Druid Clearing in Damara as retribution for betraying Strahd. Only Velinka and her niece Ezmerelda survived, though neither knows the other is alive.

RESCUE AND VISIONS: After the attack, Velinka was pulled from the wreckage by druids of the Verdant Heart and taken to a forest "that does not belong on any map." While recovering, she saw visions — "dreams woven into bark and bone" — of Barovia burning beneath an unblinking red eye. These prophetic dreams drove her to guide travelers toward Barovia when the time came.

SESSION 09 — GUIDE TO BAROVIA: Velinka guided the party through the Devil's Mists to the Gates of Barovia. She warned them to be careful around Vistani, as many serve Strahd: "Not all of us serve Strahd. Some of us remember what we were before he shackled our blood to his will. Our music once called down stars, not shadows." She opened the massive stone gates with Vistani blood but refused to enter herself, warning the party to follow the road and reach the Village of Barovia before sunset.

CURRENT STATUS: Velinka remains at the Druid Circle in Damara with the Verdant Heart druids. She believes her entire family — including Sorina and little Ezzie — died at the Druid Clearing. She does not know Ezmerelda survived and is now active in Barovia as a monster hunter.

associations.name: Gorak Broken Tusk
associations.relationship: Fellow Sea Spray crew member. Garrick joined not long after Gorak and the two became close through their shared loyalty to the crew.

associations.name: Selene Brightwater
associations.relationship: Fellow Sea Spray crew member. Part of the tight-knit family Garrick found aboard the ship.

associations.name: Captain Reaven "Emerald Eyes"
associations.relationship: Captain of the Sea Spray. Garrick was drawn in by the unlikely camaraderie aboard her ship and stayed aboard permanently.

name: Garrick Ironbrow
description: Garrick Ironbrow is a dwarven fighter and the shipwright of the Sea Spray. Stoic and immensely strong, Garrick originally boarded the ship years ago as a hired guard for a single voyage. He found himself unexpectedly drawn to the strange company of a Tabaxi captain and her orc first mate — their camaraderie was unlike anything he had known. He signed on permanently not long after Gorak joined, and has been part of the crew ever since. Garrick keeps the Sea Spray seaworthy and swings a hammer with equal skill whether he's driving nails or cracking skulls.
dm_notes:
Garrick has a tragic backstory involving pirates and revenge that drove him from his former life as a blacksmith to the sea. He doesn't talk about it, and the crew knows better than to ask. What matters to Garrick is the present — the ship, the crew, and the work.

He joined the Sea Spray not long after Gorak, initially hired as a guard for a single voyage. The unlikely friendship between a Tabaxi swashbuckler, a full-blooded orc, and a dwarven blacksmith was something Garrick never expected, but it became the closest thing to family he'd had since losing his old life. He stayed aboard and took on the role of shipwright, keeping the vessel in fighting shape.

The Sea Spray set out from Frosthaven in Vasa, carrying the party as hired protection due to rumors of fighting along the Pelavir River — King Frostmantle's wars with Narfell had made the route dangerous. During Session 02, the Night Screamer attacked. Garrick survived the fight and helped rescue Prince Ian Frostmantle from the wreckage. While the party left to find Mistress Clarissa Allyson, Garrick returned to White Bridge with the Captain and First Officer, escorting the wounded Prince and his uncle to safety from the growing reach of the Mist.

associations.name: Selene Brightwater
associations.relationship: Fellow Sea Spray crew member. Gorak sees Selene and the rest of the crew as the family he never had.

associations.name: Garrick Ironbrow
associations.relationship: Fellow Sea Spray crew member and shipwright. Part of the family Gorak found aboard the Sea Spray.

associations.name: Captain Reaven "Emerald Eyes"
associations.relationship: Captain of the Sea Spray. Reaven was the only captain who gave Gorak a chance, earning his absolute devotion. She judged him by his strength and character, not his race.

name: Gorak Broken Tusk
description: Gorak Broken Tusk is the First Mate of the Sea Spray and a towering mountain of muscle wrapped in a Blue Seaman's coat that would never button. A full-blooded orc with piercing yellow eyes and countless battle scars, Gorak wields a ship's anchor as his weapon of choice. He is disciplined despite his fearsome appearance, commanding respect through strength and unwavering loyalty. Captain Reaven was the only captain who would give him a chance and let him serve aboard her ship — a debt of trust that Gorak repays with absolute devotion. The crew of the Sea Spray became the family he never had.
dm_notes:
The Sea Spray set out from Frosthaven in Vasa, carrying the party as hired protection — King Frostmantle's wars with Narfell had made the Pelavir River route dangerous. Gorak survived the Night Screamer attack during Session 02 but took a huge bloody gash in the fight, swinging his anchor with deadly force against the creatures. After the Sea Spray was wrecked on the shore of the Pelavir River just past Bloodstone Pass, Gorak stayed behind with Captain Reaven to tend to the wounded Prince Ian Frostmantle and salvage what they could from the wreck. The party left to find Mistress Clarissa Allyson, while Gorak and the crew escorted the Prince and his uncle to White Bridge and safety from the growing reach of the Mist.

Gorak's loyalty to Emerald Eyes is absolute — she gave him something no one else would: a chance. As an orc, he was turned away from every crew and company he approached. Reaven judged him by his strength and character, not his race, and that earned her his undying loyalty. Over time, the crew — Reaven, Selene, Garrick — became the only family he has ever known.

associations.name: Gorak Broken Tusk
associations.relationship: Gorak is fiercely protective of Selene, treating her like a younger sister. He was one of the first crew members to accept her after Captain Reaven took her in.

associations.name: Garrick Ironbrow
associations.relationship: Garrick watches over Selene with gruff, paternal concern. He carved her first wand handle and pretends not to worry when her wild magic surges.

associations.name: Captain Reaven "Emerald Eyes"
associations.relationship: Captain of the Sea Spray. Reaven found Selene as a stowaway and took her in. Selene sees her as family and is deeply loyal to her.

name: Selene Brightwater
description: Selene Brightwater is the youngest member of the Sea Spray's crew — a young half-elf who looks more human than elf, with dark hair, pale skin, and striking violet eyes. Selene ran away from a cruel family that had taken her in as little more than a servant. She discovered her wild magic as a child, and the uncontrollable surges only made her captors treat her worse. When she fled, she stowed away aboard the Sea Spray. Captain Reaven was furious when she found the girl — but the more she listened to Selene's story, the softer she became. The crew adopted Selene as their own, and she has been fiercely protected by them ever since.
dm_notes:
Selene is emotionally volatile, which mirrors her wild magic — her spells surge unpredictably when she is frightened or upset. She is deeply loyal to Captain Reaven and sees the crew as the only real family she has ever known. Gorak, Garrick, and Reaven are all fiercely protective of their young ward, and anyone who threatens Selene will answer to the entire crew.

Selene is quiet and reserved around strangers but opens up quickly once she feels safe. She has a habit of tucking her hands into the sleeves of her cloak when nervous. Despite her youth and her difficult past, she is brave — she just doesn't always know it yet.

The Sea Spray set out from Frosthaven in Vasa with the party aboard as hired protection — the Pelavir River was dangerous due to King Frostmantle's wars with Narfell. Selene survived the Night Screamer attack during Session 02 and stayed behind with the rest of the crew at the wreckage on the shore of the Pelavir River. While the party left to find Mistress Clarissa Allyson, the crew escorted the wounded Prince Frostmantle and his uncle to White Bridge and safety from the growing reach of the Mist.

associations.name: Gorak Broken Tusk
associations.relationship: Reaven’s First Mate and most devoted crew member. She was the only captain who would give an orc a chance, judging him by his strength and character rather than his race. Gorak repays that trust with absolute loyalty.

associations.name: Garrick Ironbrow
associations.relationship: The Sea Spray’s shipwright. Garrick joined not long after Gorak, initially hired as a guard for a single voyage. The unlikely camaraderie aboard the Sea Spray became the closest thing to family he’d had in years.

associations.name: Selene Brightwater
associations.relationship: Reaven’s young ward. Selene stowed away aboard the Sea Spray to escape a cruel family. Reaven was furious when she found the girl, but the more she listened to Selene’s story, the softer she became. The crew adopted Selene as their own.

associations.name: Prince Ian Frostmantle
associations.relationship: Reaven and her crew escorted the gravely wounded Prince to White Bridge after the Night Screamer attack wrecked the Sea Spray.

associations.name: Lord Geoffrey Frostmantle
associations.relationship: Geoffrey returned to White Bridge with Reaven’s crew after entrusting the party with his sealed letter for Mistress Clarissa.

name: Captain Reaven "Emerald Eyes"
description: Captain Reaven is a Tabaxi swashbuckler and the captain of the Sea Spray. Silver-furred and sleek despite the wear of travel, her emerald-green eyes scan every room with the sharpness of a blade. Her movements are smooth, precise, and controlled — a predator entering a den full of prey. Known throughout the northern rivers as "Emerald Eyes," Reaven is confident, daring, and known for taking on dangerous voyages that other captains refuse. She fights with dual blades, darting between enemies with deadly precision. She commands absolute loyalty from her crew — not through fear, but through trust and the family she has built aboard her ship.
dm_notes:
BACKGROUND: Captain Reaven has a mysterious past with the Damaran rebels. She is known for dangerous voyages along the northern rivers and has built a reputation as one of the few captains willing to sail contested waters.

SESSION 01 — THE FROZEN ANCHOR: Reaven recruited the party at the Frozen Anchor tavern in Frosthaven. She entered with her crew — Gorak, Garrick, and Selene — and offered work: "The Sea Spray is sailing south along the river, and I need a crew that can handle any trouble ahead." She hired the party as protection for the voyage down the Pelavir River, which had become dangerous due to King Frostmantle’s wars with Narfell.

SESSION 02 — NIGHT SCREAMER ATTACK: During the voyage, the Sea Spray was attacked by Night Screamers. Reaven fought with deadly precision, her blades flashing as she darted between the creatures. The ship was wrecked on the shore of the Pelavir River just past Bloodstone Pass. After the battle, Reaven distributed healing potions to the party: "Consider it a gift... or perhaps an investment. If you lot are heading into that cursed city, you’re going to need every bit of help you can get."

AFTER THE WRECK: While the party left to find Mistress Clarissa Allyson in Valls, Reaven stayed behind with her crew to tend to the wounded Prince Ian Frostmantle. She and the crew escorted the Prince and Lord Geoffrey Frostmantle to White Bridge and safety from the growing reach of the Mist.

LEADERSHIP STYLE: Reaven commands through trust rather than authority. She gave Gorak a chance when no one else would, took in Selene as a stowaway and adopted her into the crew, and earned Garrick’s lifelong loyalty through genuine camaraderie. She smirks rather than getting angry, and her voice is "smooth but firm, cutting through silence like a well-honed dagger." She also reminded the party to be cautious about unsanctioned magic use under Damaran law.

associations.name: Lord Geoffrey Frostmantle
associations.relationship: Brennor served in Lord Geoffrey's retinue during the journey to Valls.

associations.name: Prince Ian Frostmantle
associations.relationship: Brennor is sworn to the Prince's service. He led survivors to White Bridge hoping to reunite with the Prince.

associations.name: Father Alric
associations.relationship: Father Alric was killed by Kaelin Stormraven. After his death, Brennor took command of the survivors.

name: Ser Brennor Cale
description: Ser Brennor Cale is a paladin and knight sworn to the Frostmantle dynasty. He was among Prince Ian Frostmantle's retinue during the journey to Valls and one of the few knights to survive the undead ambush. He made it to the abandoned church where he and other survivors sheltered. After Father Alric was killed by Kaelin Stormraven, Brennor took command of the remaining survivors from Valls and led them to White Bridge in hopes of reuniting with the Prince and Lord Geoffrey Frostmantle.
dm_notes: Ser Brennor was part of Lord Geoffrey Frostmantle's party of 60 men (20 knights and 40 men-at-arms) that crossed the river north of Valls. After the undead ambush led by a dark rider decimated the group, Brennor was one of the few knights who reached the abandoned church where the party later found them during Sessions 03-04. When Father Alric was killed by Kaelin Stormraven, Brennor assumed responsibility for the surviving civilians and soldiers from Valls and led them to White Bridge to seek safety and await word from the Prince and his uncle.

associations.name: Milivoj
associations.relationship: Henrik will manipulate the desperate gravedigger Milivoj into stealing the Bones of Saint Andral from the church, removing the holy protection that keeps Strahd and his forces out.

associations.name: Strahd Von Zarovich
associations.relationship: Henrik has been coerced by Strahd’s agents into servitude. He lives in constant terror, forced to hide vampire spawn and Blood Hunters in the attic of his shop as Strahd prepares to breach Vallaki’s walls.

name: Henrik Van der Voort
description: Henrik Van der Voort is the coffin maker of Vallaki — a nervous, thin, perpetually exhausted man who lives and works alone in his shop among the narrow streets of town. He avoids eye contact, jumps at sudden noises, and clearly hides some terrible secret. Henrik is not evil — just terrified and cornered. He has been coerced by Strahd’s agents into hiding creatures in the storage loft above his workshop, and he hasn’t slept in days.
dm_notes:
CURRENT STATE: Henrik has been coerced by Strahd’s agents into hiding vampire spawn and Blood Hunters (werewolves) in the storage loft above his workshop. The loft feels heavy, watchful, and unnaturally still. Henrik lives in constant terror, knowing the creatures above could descend and kill him at any moment, but is too afraid of Strahd’s retribution to seek help or flee. He acted under threat, not loyalty.

UPCOMING — BONES OF SAINT ANDRAL: Strahd’s agents will manipulate Henrik into convincing the gravedigger Milivoj to steal the sacred Bones of Saint Andral from the Church of St. Andral. The bones are the spiritual lynchpin of Vallaki’s resistance — while they remain in the church, the building is consecrated ground that Strahd and his spawn cannot enter. Their removal will break the church’s protection and leave Vallaki vulnerable.

UPCOMING — VALLAKI FALLS: The theft of the bones and the hidden forces in Henrik’s attic are both part of Strahd’s plan to breach the walls of Vallaki. The spawn and Blood Hunters concealed in shipping crates in the loft will deploy when the time comes, striking from inside the town while Strahd’s external forces attack. Henrik’s shop is a critical staging point for the fall of the town.

ROLEPLAY: Henrik hasn’t slept in days. Neighbors whisper about strange noises from his shop. If confronted, he may break down and confess — or the creatures in the loft may attack first. He is a broken man, not a villain.

associations.name: Henrik Van der Voort
associations.relationship: Milivoj will be manipulated by Henrik into stealing the sacred Bones of Saint Andral from the church, removing the holy protection that keeps Strahd out.

name: Milivoj
description: Milivoj is a young gravedigger at the Church of St. Andral in Vallaki. He is scrawny, overworked, and perpetually dirty from digging graves. Milivoj struggles to feed his younger siblings and is desperate enough to take on any work that pays.
dm_notes:
CURRENT STATE: Milivoj has not yet stolen the bones. He is a desperate young man trying to feed his siblings, working as a gravedigger’s apprentice at the Church of St. Andral under Father Lucian Petrovich.

UPCOMING — BONES OF SAINT ANDRAL: Henrik Van der Voort, acting under orders from Strahd’s agents, will manipulate Milivoj into stealing the sacred Bones of Saint Andral from the church. Milivoj’s desperation to feed his family will make him vulnerable to Henrik’s offer of coin. The theft will remove the holy protection that prevents Strahd and his forces from entering consecrated ground — a critical step in Strahd’s plan to bring about the fall of Vallaki.

AFTERMATH: Once the theft is done, Milivoj will be guilt-ridden but terrified of the consequences. He is a pawn, not a conspirator — he has no idea what the bones truly protect or what Strahd plans to do once they are removed.

associations.name: Ireena Kolyana
associations.relationship: Kolyan's adopted daughter. He found her as a young child wandering the Svalich Woods after a dire wolf attack separated her from her biological family. He raised her as his own alongside Ismark.

associations.name: Ismark Kolyanovich
associations.relationship: Kolyan's biological son. Ismark inherited the burden of Burgomaster after Kolyan's death and carries the weight of protecting his sister.

associations.name: Strahd Von Zarovich
associations.relationship: Kolyan wrote a desperate letter pleading for help against Strahd's attacks on his home. Strahd's repeated visits to claim Ireena drove Kolyan to his death from sheer terror and exhaustion.

associations.name: Father Donavich
associations.relationship: The village priest who presided over Kolyan's funeral at the church in the Village of Barovia.

associations.name: Baron Dmitri Krezkov
associations.relationship: Dmitri was a close friend and fellow burgomaster. Kolyan's death was a blow to Dmitri, who saw him as one of the few leaders in Barovia who genuinely cared about his people.

name: Kolyan Indirovich
description: Kolyan Indirovich was the Burgomaster of the Village of Barovia and the father of Ismark and adoptive father of Ireena. A good and honorable man, Kolyan spent his final days barricading his home against Strahd's nightly assaults as the vampire lord came to claim Ireena. The relentless siege broke Kolyan's health and spirit, and he died of a heart attack brought on by fright. His death left his children to face Strahd's wrath alone and set the campaign's events in motion.
dm_notes:
Kolyan's name follows the Barovian patronymic tradition — 'Indirovich' means 'son of Indir,' his father. His children carry his name forward: Ismark Kolyanovich ('son of Kolyan') and Ireena Kolyana ('daughter of Kolyan'). There is no family surname.

Kolyan found the young Ireena wandering at the edge of the Svalich Woods as a small child after a dire wolf attack scattered her biological family. He took her in and raised her as his own daughter alongside Ismark, never telling her the truth of her origins. Her biological brother Izek was separated during the same attack and eventually ended up in Vallaki, taken in by the Vallakovich household.

Kolyan was close friends with Baron Vargas Vallakovich and the other burgomasters of Barovia. The two families visited each other regularly, and Kolyan's children attended the Festival of Light in Vallaki as honoured guests. This close bond is why Ismark was certain Ireena would find safety with the Vallakoviches.

Kolyan was a descendant of Ismark the Great, a legendary Barovian hero, which is why the villagers mockingly call his son 'Ismark the Lesser.' Despite the impossible situation, Kolyan refused to surrender Ireena to Strahd. The forged letter bearing his name — the one that lured the adventurers to Barovia — was actually written by Strahd to draw fresh prey into his domain.

At campaign start, Kolyan's body lies in the family home awaiting burial. Ismark asks the party to help escort the coffin to the church for a proper funeral with Father Donavich.

associations.name: Parriwimple
associations.relationship: Bildrath's nephew and enforcer at the shop. Dimwitted but massively strong, Parriwimple does the heavy lifting and intimidates anyone who might cause trouble.

name: Bildrath Cantemir
description: Bildrath Cantemir is the owner of the only general store in the Village of Barovia. He is a greedy, self-serving man who gouges prices mercilessly — charging ten times the normal rate for basic supplies because he knows his customers have no alternative. Bildrath views the misery of Barovia as a business opportunity and shows no sympathy for those who cannot afford his prices. His massive nephew Parriwimple serves as both stock boy and enforcer.
dm_notes: Bildrath is universally disliked but tolerated because his shop is the only source of equipment and supplies in the village. He refuses to negotiate and will call Parriwimple to deal with anyone who tries to steal or threaten him. Despite his greed, he is a coward who will capitulate if genuinely threatened with violence. He has no loyalty to Strahd or anyone else — only to his own profit.

associations.name: Bildrath Cantemir
associations.relationship: Parriwimple's uncle and employer. Bildrath uses Parriwimple's strength to run the shop and intimidate customers.

name: Parriwimple
description: Parriwimple is Bildrath Cantemir's nephew — a hulking, simple-minded young man of immense physical strength. He works at his uncle's general store hauling crates, stocking shelves, and serving as an unspoken threat to anyone who might cause trouble. Despite his intimidating size, Parriwimple is gentle and childlike in demeanor. He genuinely wants to help people and is easily befriended with kind words or small gifts.
dm_notes: Parriwimple is far stronger than he looks — easily capable of overpowering most adventurers in a grapple. However, he has no desire to fight and will only become violent if his uncle is directly threatened. He is easily manipulated by anyone who shows him kindness, which Bildrath exploits constantly. If befriended, Parriwimple can be a useful source of simple, honest information about the village — he says what he sees without guile or filter.

associations.name: Luna E'Tressa
associations.relationship: Sarkov's wife. Luna speaks for them both since Sarkov lost his tongue. They gave up the Vistani traveling life together when they married.

associations.name: Magda E'Tressa
associations.relationship: Sarkov's widowed aunt who handles cooking at the inn. Fiercely protective of her nephew.

associations.name: Strahd Von Zarovich
associations.relationship: Strahd had Sarkov's tongue cut out for speaking against the vampire lord's will. This act of cruelty drove Sarkov and Luna to abandon their Vistani caravan.

name: Sarkov E'Tressa
location: Village of Barovia (Blood of the Vine Inn)
description: Sarkov E'Tressa is the co-owner of the Blood of the Vine Inn in the Village of Barovia. A broad-shouldered, silent man in his late 40s, Sarkov communicates entirely through gestures and steady presence — his tongue was cut out for speaking against Strahd. Originally from the Tser Hill Vistani, Sarkov and his wife Luna gave up the Travel when they married and settled in the village as innkeepers, their views no longer aligned with the caravan's deference to Strahd.
dm_notes:
Sarkov is watchful and protective. He runs the inn's bar with quiet efficiency, and regulars understand his gestures and expressions well enough to communicate. He harbors a deep, silent hatred for Strahd but is pragmatic enough to know that open defiance means death. The party first met Sarkov on arrival in the Village of Barovia — Gregor awkwardly discovered his missing tongue while trying to converse with him.

The E'Tressa family are originally from the Tser Hill Vistani but gave up the nomadic life when Sarkov married Luna, who was from the Village of Barovia. Their decision to settle down and abandon the Travel put them at odds with their caravan, and they now live in exile from their former community.

associations.name: Sarkov E'Tressa
associations.relationship: Luna's husband. She speaks for them both since Sarkov cannot. They gave up the Vistani traveling life when they married.

associations.name: Ilyana Kostova
associations.relationship: Luna's godmother, who followed the family into exile at the inn.

associations.name: Klara Vorovich
associations.relationship: Luna's distant cousin and the inn's bookkeeper. Unknown to Luna, Klara secretly spies for Strahd.

name: Luna E'Tressa
location: Village of Barovia (Blood of the Vine Inn)
description: Luna E'Tressa is the co-owner of the Blood of the Vine Inn and the voice of the establishment. A striking woman in her early 40s with kind but weary eyes, Luna was born in the Village of Barovia and married Sarkov of the Tser Hill Vistani. When Sarkov's tongue was cut out by Strahd's order, the couple abandoned the Travel and settled in her home village to run the inn. Luna was once a singer among the Vistani, and her warm voice still carries the cadence of old caravan songs. She speaks for both herself and Sarkov, translating his gestures for newcomers.
dm_notes:
Luna is the heart of the Blood of the Vine. She manages the inn's guests, mediates disputes, and keeps the extended family functioning. She is warm but exhausted by the weight of their exile and the constant oppression of life in Barovia. She knows more about the village's secrets than she lets on — years of running the only inn in town means she hears everything.

Her marriage to Sarkov was a love match that cost them both their Vistani community. The Tser Hill Vistani viewed their departure as a betrayal, and the couple has had no contact with their former caravan since settling in the village.

associations.name: Sarkov E'Tressa
associations.relationship: Magda's nephew. She followed him into exile and fiercely protects him and Luna.

name: Magda E'Tressa
location: Village of Barovia (Blood of the Vine Inn)
description: Magda E'Tressa is Sarkov's widowed aunt and the cook at the Blood of the Vine Inn. A stout woman in her late 60s with a hooked nose and a cane she doesn't truly need, Magda is gruff, practical, and scolds patrons like unruly children. She followed her nephew into exile from the Tser Hill Vistani and has appointed herself the family's fierce protector. Her cooking is simple Barovian fare — heavy stews, black bread, and whatever root vegetables survive the cursed soil — but it keeps the inn running.
dm_notes: Magda uses her cane more as a prop and occasional weapon than a walking aid. She is sharper than she appears and has a keen sense for trouble. She will fiercely defend Sarkov and Luna from anyone she perceives as a threat. Magda left the Tser Hill Vistani without hesitation when Sarkov was mutilated — family loyalty runs deeper than any caravan bond for her.

associations.name: Luna E'Tressa
associations.relationship: Ilyana is Luna's godmother. She dotes on Luna and followed the family into exile.

name: Ilyana Kostova
location: Village of Barovia (Blood of the Vine Inn)
description: Ilyana Kostova is Luna E'Tressa's godmother and a longtime fixture at the Blood of the Vine Inn. A tall, wiry woman in her early 70s who drapes herself in bright scarves, Ilyana was once a singer and dancer among the Tser Hill Vistani. Her voice has gone raspy with age, but she still hums old caravan tunes while she cleans. She claims to have 'second sight' — the ability to sense the presence of evil and read omens in ordinary events. Most dismiss it as superstition, though her warnings have an unsettling habit of proving accurate.
dm_notes: Ilyana's 'second sight' is left deliberately ambiguous — she may genuinely have a minor gift of divination, or she may simply be a perceptive old woman who reads people well. Either way, she provides atmospheric flavor and can serve as a cryptic information source. She knows the old Vistani stories and traditions, and her warnings about roads, weather, and strangers carry weight with the inn's regulars even if they roll their eyes.

associations.name: Luna E'Tressa
associations.relationship: Klara is Luna's distant cousin. Luna trusts her completely, unaware of her treachery.

associations.name: Strahd Von Zarovich
associations.relationship: Klara secretly passes information about inn patrons to Vistani loyalists who report directly to Strahd.

associations.name: Arrigal Vanduva
associations.relationship: Klara passes her intelligence through Vistani loyalist channels that ultimately reach Arrigal and Strahd's spy network.

name: Klara Vorovich
location: Village of Barovia (Blood of the Vine Inn)
description: Klara Vorovich is Luna E'Tressa's distant cousin and the bookkeeper at the Blood of the Vine Inn. A thin, severe woman in her late 60s with long gray hair always tied back in a tight bun, Klara serves drinks with a forced smile and keeps the inn's ledgers in meticulous order. She is quiet, efficient, and always seems to be listening.
dm_notes:
Klara is a spy for Strahd — she carefully observes every traveler who passes through the inn and passes her intelligence to Vistani loyalists who report to Strahd's network. She never fully abandoned her loyalty to the Vistani's traditional service to Strahd. While the rest of the E'Tressa family broke with the caravan, Klara followed them to the village as an embedded informant.

Klara is the reason Strahd always seems to know when strangers arrive in the Village of Barovia. She is calculating, patient, and careful — she has maintained her cover for years without arousing suspicion from her own family. If exposed, she will attempt to flee to the Vistani camps rather than fight.

This is a potential plot twist for the party — discovering that even the 'safe haven' of the Blood of the Vine has Strahd's eyes and ears inside it.

associations.name: Morgantha Wormwiggle
associations.relationship: Bella's mother and the matriarch of the Bonegrinder coven. Morgantha leads the coven and handles the sale of dream pastries.

associations.name: Offalia Wormwiggle
associations.relationship: Bella's daughter and the youngest member of the coven. Offalia is the most openly cruel of the three.

name: Bella Wormwiggle
description: Bella Wormwiggle appears as a hunched, middle-aged woman with stringy hair and a gap-toothed smile. She can be found at the Old Bonegrinder windmill alongside her mother and daughter, tending to the 'baking.' Bella is quieter than her mother Morgantha but watches visitors with unsettling intensity.
dm_notes:
Bella is a night hag and the middle generation of the Bonegrinder coven. She handles the grim work of processing the stolen children's life force into the dream pastry dough. Bella is pragmatic and methodical where Morgantha is cunning and Offalia is sadistic — she views the harvesting of children as simply the family trade.

In her true hag form, Bella is gaunt and terrible, with clawed hands stained dark from her work. She is the most dangerous of the three in direct combat, favoring her claws and the coven's shared spellcasting. The party encountered the coven at Old Bonegrinder during Sessions 17-18.

associations.name: Morgantha Wormwiggle
associations.relationship: Offalia's grandmother and the matriarch of the Bonegrinder coven.

associations.name: Bella Wormwiggle
associations.relationship: Offalia's mother and fellow coven member. Bella does most of the pastry preparation while Offalia handles the children.

name: Offalia Wormwiggle
description: Offalia Wormwiggle appears as a young gril around the age of 10-12 years with a nervous giggle and fidgeting hands. She often goes with her grandmother to sell pies and charms the locals with her smile..
dm_notes:
Offalia is a night hag and the youngest member of the Bonegrinder coven — Morgantha's granddaughter and Bella's daughter. She is the most openly sadistic of the three, taking particular delight in tormenting the kidnapped children before they are ground into dream pastry ingredients. Offalia keeps the children caged on the upper floor of the windmill and 'plays' with them in ways that would horrify even hardened adventurers.

Despite her cruelty, Offalia is the weakest link in the coven — she is the most likely to panic if the coven is attacked and may try to flee rather than fight if separated from her mother and grandmother. She is the one who interacts with the other children the most, and is the one that slips the a treat to help her Grandmother or Mother take them.

associations.name: Iskander
associations.relationship: Duplicate of Yuri. Helps run Skanders Imporium of Magic.

associations.name: Eskander
associations.relationship: Duplicate of Yuri. Helps run Skanders Imporium of Magic.

associations.name: Oskander
associations.relationship: Duplicate of Yuri. Married Mary Strazni and was murdered by Rahadin.

associations.name: Askander
associations.relationship: Duplicate of Yuri. Runs the Alchemy shop in Vallaki.

associations.name: Uskander
associations.relationship: Duplicate of Yuri. Runs the Antique store in Vallaki.

associations.name: Mad Mary Strazni
associations.relationship: Mary was Yuri's young apprentice. She accidentally triggered the amulet of wishing that created the Skander duplicates.

name: Yuri Skander
description: Yuri Skander is a respected wizard who runs Skanders Imporium of Magic in Vallaki, buying and selling much of the magical merchandise that the Tser Hill Vistani bring into town from beyond the Mists. He is the 'Prime' Skander — the original — from whom five duplicates were created by a magical accident involving an amulet of wishing.
dm_notes:
Yuri was a respected wizard whose young apprentice Mary Strazni accidentally triggered an amulet of wishing — a pendant with a single copper coin enclosed in amber. While studying it, Mary expressed a wish that there were more men like Yuri in Vallaki. The resulting flash created five duplicates of Yuri, each with all his memories and abilities. They decided Yuri should remain the Prime Skander, and the duplicates took new names: Iskander, Askander, Uskander, Eskander, and Oskander. Over the years, each became their own person with distinct interests and lives.

Yuri, Iskander, and Eskander continue to run the Imporium together. When Rahadin murdered Oskander, the Skanders vowed never to forgive Strahd. The entire Skander family now harbors a deep hatred for the vampire lord and his servants.

associations.name: Yuri Skander
associations.relationship: The Prime Skander, from whom Iskander was duplicated.

name: Iskander
description: Iskander is one of the five duplicates of Yuri Skander, created by the accidental triggering of an amulet of wishing. He continues to work alongside Yuri and Eskander at Skanders Imporium of Magic in Vallaki.
dm_notes: Iskander retains all of Yuri's original memories and magical abilities but has developed into his own person over the years. He helps run the Imporium and shares the other Skanders' hatred of Strahd after Rahadin murdered their brother Oskander.

associations.name: Yuri Skander
associations.relationship: The Prime Skander, from whom Askander was duplicated.

name: Askander
description: Askander is one of the five duplicates of Yuri Skander who took up alchemy after the duplication. He owns and operates the Alchemy shop in Vallaki and has become very skilled at his craft.
dm_notes: Askander diverged from the other Skanders by pursuing alchemy rather than general wizardry. He is very good at it at this point and his shop is a valuable resource in Vallaki. He shares the Skanders' hatred of Strahd after Rahadin murdered their brother Oskander.

associations.name: Yuri Skander
associations.relationship: The Prime Skander, from whom Uskander was duplicated.

name: Uskander
description: Uskander is one of the five duplicates of Yuri Skander who developed a love for all things ancient. He runs the Antique store in Vallaki and is a knowledgeable scholar of Barovian history and artifacts.
dm_notes:
Uskander became close friends with Nikolai Wachter, bonding over their shared love of history and antiquities. However, when it was learned that Nikolai was associating with Strahd — the master of Rahadin, who killed Oskander — Uskander broke off the friendship. This happened shortly before Nikolai was murdered while traveling to investigate ruins to the south near Mount Ghakis.

Uskander now runs the Antique store in Vallaki and shares the Skanders' hatred of Strahd. His knowledge of ancient artifacts and Barovian history makes him a potentially valuable resource for the party.

dm_notes: Eskander retains all of Yuri's original memories and magical abilities but has developed into his own person over the years. He helps run the Imporium and shares the other Skanders' hatred of Strahd after Rahadin murdered their brother Oskander.

name: Oskander
description: Oskander was one of the five duplicates of Yuri Skander. Unlike his brothers who pursued magic and commerce, Oskander fell in love with Mary Strazni — Yuri's young apprentice — and married her. They had a daughter, Gertrude, whom they both loved dearly.
dm_notes:
Oskander was the Skander duplicate who chose love over magic. He married Mary Strazni and they had a daughter, Gertrude. Rahadin murdered Oskander in a fit of rage — nobody is certain what their fight was about or why Rahadin killed him. His death devastated Mary, who eventually left Vallaki and returned to the Village of Barovia with Gertrude, where she became known as Mad Mary.

Once word of Oskander's murder reached the other Skanders, they vowed never to forgive Strahd — the master Rahadin serves. Oskander's death turned the entire Skander family into bitter enemies of Castle Ravenloft.

At the Festival of Light, Nikolai protected Elvir Martikov — Urwin's youngest daughter — during Strahd's attack. The two have feelings for each other. This connection between the Wachter and Martikov families could prove significant.

Nikolai is aware his mother has her Narfell practices but pays them little mind. He is unaware she keeps his father's preserved corpse in her bedroom.

name: Karl Wachter

dm_notes:
Karl takes after his late father Nikolai Wachter in his love of books and scholarship. He spends time in the Wachterhaus library his father built, continuing the family tradition of historical study.

At the Festival of Light, Karl tried to protect his younger sister Stella from the attacking minions of Lady Williams but was unable to save her. He feels responsible for her death and the guilt weighs heavily on him.

name: Kiara Toranescu
description: Kiara Toranescu is the Den Mother of the Barovian werewolf packs — a druid and healer who serves as the spiritual heart of the Den. She is Jiro's grandmother and the mother of the late Den Leader Zuleika. She approaches outsiders peacefully and made a deal with the adventurers on behalf of the Den.
dm_notes:
Kiara is the mother of the late Zuleika Toranescu and wife of Duesius. She has served as Den Mother for decades, tending to the wounded, mediating disputes between packs, and teaching the younger wolves. Like her husband and daughter-in-law Emil, she does not want to continue the war with humans.

When the players came to the Werewolf Den in Session 21, it was Kiara who approached them peacefully with the words 'Be at ease — there is one here who would speak to you.' She and Duesius negotiated a deal with the players on behalf of the Den. After Emil returned from the Wizard's Tower battle, she learned of the deal and chose to honor it.

Kiara is fiercely protective of her grandson Jiro, who has already lost his father and older brothers to human hunters.

dm_notes:
Duesius is the patriarch of the Toranescu family. He lost his son Zuleika and grandson Ekrol to Elandra Stormraven's assassination plot. Despite this, he does not seek blind revenge — like his wife Kiara, he believes the packs have lost too much already.

Duesius helped negotiate the deal with the players at the Werewolf Den in Session 21. An Insight check reveals the compassion, pride, and humor in his eyes as he watches his grandson Jiro, the last male heir of the Toranescu line.

name: Jiro Toranescu
description: Jiro Toranescu is a young werewolf boy who has suffered tremendous loss — his father Zuleika and older brothers were killed, and his mother Emil was believed dead after the fight at the Wizard's Tower. He is fierce, angry, and heartbroken.
dm_notes:
Jiro lost his father Zuleika and older brothers Ekrol to violence. His mother Emil led the attack on the Wizard's Tower under Elandra's orders and was believed killed when she jumped from a tower window to escape the players. When the players arrived at the Werewolf Den in Session 21, Jiro charged Brother Ivan with a kitchen knife — tears streaking down his face, but hatred and rage in his eyes.

If the players spared Jiro, Kiara explained why the child was angry. Jiro kicked Ivan in the chin before running deeper into the cave.

Unknown to Jiro and the Den at the time, his mother Emil survived the fall and returned after the players left. Jiro is the last young heir of the Toranescu pack and his grandparents are fiercely protective of him.

name: Anna Krezkova
description: Anna Krezkova is the wife of Baron Dmitri Krezkov, burgomaster of Krezk. She is grieving the death of their daughter Ilya but remains practical and steady — the kind of person who acts when others freeze. Anna is a respectable sorceress, having studied with Lady Fiona Wachter.
dm_notes:
Anna is the steady hand behind the Krezkov household. While Dmitri leads with caution and duty, Anna leads with action and composure. She is grieving the loss of their daughter Ilya alongside Dmitri, but her grief has not broken her — if anything, it has made her sharper.

Anna is a respectable sorceress, having studied with Lady Fiona Wachter. The two women share a bond deepened by shared loss — Anna continues to help Fiona grieve the death of Stella, having recently lost her own child.

At the Festival of Light in Vallaki, Anna and Dmitri were honoured guests watching the proceedings with the other burgomasters and their families. When Strahd attacked, Anna was the one who physically got Lady Fiona Wachter moving after Fiona broke down following Stella's death. While others froze, Anna did not hesitate.

Anna is a practical ally — calm, observant, and steady under pressure.

name: Vasilka
description: Vasilka is a flesh golem created by the Abbot using the body and essence of Ilya Krezkov, the daughter of Baron Dmitri Krezkov. Also referred to as 'the Resurrected Ilya Krezkov,' Vasilka was built to serve as Strahd's bride. The Abbot thinks of Vasilka as his daughter — an innocent child made to appease Strahd. She is a powerful Undead/Construct Sorceress with Lair Actions and special combat actions.
dm_notes:
Vasilka is fiercely loyal to the Abbot and to Strahd, as she was created to serve him. She wore the Holy Symbol of Ravenkind as a gift from her Father/Creator until the Abbot was forced to rip it from her neck and hand it to the players during Sessions 22-23. This act caused Vasilka to drop to the ground, and when she woke she was angered that these people would force her Father to give up such a powerful relic.

Vasilka led an assault on the Tser Hill Vistani camp with Patchwork Goblins and Direwolves during Sessions 27-28. She demonstrated terrifying power — taking control of Thorian's water spell and hurling it back over the defenders on the hilltop. She has what feels like an unlimited supply of Mongrelfolk/Patchwork Goblins at her disposal. This is the current battle the players are in.

Prior to Tser Hill, Vasilka and the Abbot's forces overwhelmed the Vistani at Tser Raven in the middle of the night, killing any they could and burning their wagons. The surviving members fled into the woods or to shelter in Krezk.

Vasilka can potentially be recruited as an ally if the players kill the Abbot without harming her or her mongrelfolk. She would want to be free and for her kind to be left alone in the Abbey in exchange for their aid.

name: Mordenkainen
description: Mordenkainen is a legendary archmage from the world of Oerth. He came to Barovia a year ago at the request of his old friend Rudolph Van Richten to help defeat Strahd and the Stormraven Sisters. After a failed assault on Castle Ravenloft that left him broken and mad, he spent ten months wandering the northern woods near Mount Baratok, attacking anything that came close. He was recently found and restored by Van Richten and Ezmerelda.
dm_notes:
Mordenkainen arrived in Barovia roughly one year before the players, about six months ahead of Van Richten. Van Richten had called his old friend in to help destroy Strahd and the Stormraven Sisters for Ezmerelda, whose family was killed by them. Mordenkainen is fond of Ezmerelda, treating her like a niece. She calls him 'Uncle Mordy.' It did not take much convincing to bring him to Barovia.

While Mordenkainen was building alliances and preparing for the assault, Klara Vorovich, a spy at the Blood of the Vine Inn, reported his activities through Vistani loyalist channels to Strahd. With his plans exposed, Mordenkainen had no choice but to act before he was ready. He rallied what allies he had: Doru, Ireena, Ismark, and about fifty villagers, and launched a desperate assault on Castle Ravenloft.

The assault failed. On the ramparts, Strahd descended in person. When he saw Ireena, he faltered for a single heartbeat, giving Mordenkainen his chance. The wizard struck Strahd with a devastating spell that gravely wounded him. But Strahd recovered and struck Mordenkainen down, pushing him over the edge of the castle walls. He fell into the valley below.

Mordenkainen survived the fall but lost his spellbook and magical focus. The impact and Strahd's attack shattered his mind. He could not remember who he was or why he was so badly injured. For the last ten months, he has been wandering the northern woods around Mount Baratok, feral and dangerous, attacking anything and anyone that came close. Strahd believes him dead.

Van Richten and Ezmerelda tracked him down and restored him with a Greater Restoration spell (referenced in Session 27 wrap-up). He is described as confused about what happened but 'his same stubborn self.' They are heading back to town and should arrive in two days.

Mordenkainen is stubborn, brilliant, and does not suffer fools. Without his spellbook and focus, he is operating at reduced power. His 8th and 9th level spell slots are unavailable. The DM may restore them when his spellbook is recovered or at a major story milestone. Even weakened, he is the most powerful spellcaster the party has access to. His Staff of Power survived the fall.
